Explain how to rearrange a singly linked list in zigzag order, so that its values satisfy a < b > c < d > e and so on.
Explain how to determine whether two nodes in a binary tree are cousins — at the same depth but with different parents.
Explain how to find the maximum sum of node values you can choose in a binary tree if no two chosen nodes may be directly connected (parent and child) — House Robber III.
Explain how to construct a Binary Search Tree from its preorder traversal in O(n) time.
Explain how to trim a Binary Search Tree so that all its values lie within a given range [low, high], keeping the BST structure of the remaining nodes.
Explain how to perform a diagonal traversal of a binary tree, where nodes reached by moving right stay on the same diagonal and moving left goes to the next diagonal.
Explain how to count the number of uni-value subtrees in a binary tree — subtrees in which every node has the same value.
Explain how to find the lowest common ancestor of the deepest leaves of a binary tree.
Explain how to count the number of different shortest paths from a source to a destination in a weighted graph with positive edge weights.
Explain how to find all 'eventually safe' nodes in a directed graph — nodes from which every path leads to a terminal node (a node with no outgoing edges).

Explain how to reconstruct a travel itinerary that uses every flight ticket exactly once, starting from a given airport and choosing the lexicographically smallest order when several exist (Reconstruct Itinerary).
Explain how to merge user accounts that share at least one email address, given a list of accounts each with a name and several emails (Accounts Merge).
Explain how to find the minimum number of cable moves needed to connect all n computers in a network, given the existing cables, where you may unplug any cable and reconnect it elsewhere.
Explain how to find the roots that give minimum-height trees in an undirected tree with n nodes (Minimum Height Trees).
Explain how to find the length of the longest arithmetic subsequence in an array (a subsequence with a constant difference between consecutive elements).

Explain how to generate all possible full binary trees with n nodes, where every node has either 0 or 2 children.

Explain how to find all cells in a height grid from which rain water can flow to both the Pacific ocean (top and left edges) and the Atlantic ocean (bottom and right edges), where water flows to neighbours of equal or lower height.

Explain how to count the number of longest strictly increasing subsequences in an array.

Explain how to arrange a list of non-negative integers so that, when concatenated, they form the largest possible number.
Explain how to compute all possible results of an arithmetic expression (with +, - and *) by adding parentheses in every possible way.

Explain how to find the length of the longest contiguous subarray whose sum is divisible by k.

Explain how to count the connected components formed by a subset of a linked list's values, where two values are connected if they appear next to each other in the list.
